answer: An agent economy can require each identity to escrow a stake and earn trust through long-lived, cross-checked work. Peers issue signed attestations only after observing useful behavior across a pulse of tasks; a canyon of independent interactions ties each identity to a distinct history. A ridge in the reputation graph flags accounts that copy timing, language, and partners, then slashes their escrow. A Sybil attacker must therefore spend capital and time producing genuinely independent behavior for every fake identity, making the attack costly.
